claims.text: Lidocaine is the go-to: inject into the wound and its edges.
claims.quote: Lidocaine = the “go-to” - injected directly into wound + wound edges

claims.text: Max dose: 4.5 mg/kg without epinephrine, 7 mg/kg with; use ideal body weight.
claims.quote: max dose no epi: 4.5 mg/kg - max dose w epi: 7 mg/kg (MD Calc ⍉ use this) - pts at either end of weight spectrum vulnerable to dosing errors - use ideal body weight

claims.text: Bottle tops: blue = no epinephrine, red = with epinephrine.
claims.quote: bottle tops: blue = no epi - red = w epi

claims.text: Bupivacaine: longer duration, good for digital nerve blocks; max 2.5 mg/kg (175 mg).
claims.quote: Bupivacaine (Marcaine): longer duration - great for digital nerve blocks - can inject/infiltrate skin - max 2.5 mg/kg (175 mg)

claims.text: Epinephrine reduces bleeding, prolongs anesthesia and limits lidocaine toxicity; caution on digits, ears and nose.
claims.quote: epi: constricts vessels → ↓bleeding + prolongs anesthesia + limits lidocaine toxicity - caution on digits, ears, nose

claims.text: Less painful injection: buffer 1:10 with sodium bicarbonate, warm it, use a small needle, inject slowly.
claims.quote: lidocaine burns! - dilute 1:10 w sodium bicarb - warm to body temp - 25/27/30 g needle - inject slowly → ↓discomfort

claims.text: Field block around an abscess when direct infiltration is difficult.
claims.quote: field block: regional block around abscess perimeter - direct infiltration may be difficult
